title: Midday shift handoff — latency spike playbook (2026-03-10)
content:
Context:
Today’s midday shift observed a transient latency spike across the US-hosted inference pool during the 11:15–11:45 PDT window. This doc is a compact handoff + triage playbook for the midday shift team and for the release train that intersects with hotfix cadence. It captures timeline, immediate mitigations, decisions, and follow-ups for the next release window.

Goals for this doc:
- Capture what we did and why (so on-call and release leads can act).
- Provide a checklist for packaging a minimal hotfix if needed.
- Define canary thresholds and rollback criteria for the dedicated release train.

Summary (short):
- Impact: 11:15–11:44 PDT, 4.7% of requests in us-west experienced >500ms tail latency increases (p95 unchanged). No increased error rate.
- Trigger: elevated GPU-side queuing on a small subset of instances behind load balancer A (suspected kernel scheduling regression after kernel bump on 03/09).
- Immediate mitigation: temporarily moved 10% traffic off the affected pool to fallback nodes in us-east, reduced max-batch-size from 16->8 for affected model family, rebalanced KV cache policy.
- Decision: proceed with controlled hotfix branch that reverts kernel scheduling flag and patches autoscaler probe; target ship in the next hotfix window (18:00 PDT) unless further anomalies.

Timeline (local times PDT):
- 11:12 - Alert: latency spike alerted via PagerDuty (PD rule: p99 > 800ms for 5m).
- 11:14 - Duty engineer (Marcus) acknowledges and posts initial triage in #release-engineering.
- 11:15 - Quick check: error rates OK, CPU/GPU utilization reported 78% on average, but queuing latencies on 6 nodes spiked.
- 11:20 - Roll traffic: routed ~10% of traffic via smart-router fallback to healthy pool in us-east (automatic fallback policy engaged).
- 11:24 - Reduce batch size to mitigate GPU queue growth for model x-small-v1. Dropped from 16 to 8; immediate improvement in tail observed.
- 11:30 - Engineering lead (Sophie) convenes warroom; decision to continue mitigations and prepare hotfix branch that reverts kernel-scheduling-change-2026-03-09.
- 11:44 - Latency trend recovered to baseline p95/p99 within 10% of pre-incident. Monitoring continues.

Immediate actions taken (owners):
- Marcus Patel: routed 10% traffic to fallback pool and posted perf graphs in thread. (done)
- Ava Thompson: changed model config max_batch_size from 16->8 for affected model family and verified telemetry. (done)
- Diego Morales: collected kernel logs and node-level traces from affected hosts; uploaded to GH artifact bundle. (done)
- Priya Rao: prepared hotfix branch (revert kernel-scheduling flag + autoscaler probe timeout tweak) and opened PR RE-HOTFIX-198. (in progress)

Triage notes and hypothesis:
- Root hypothesis: kernel scheduling parameter changed in node image on 2026-03-09 (image: gpu-runtime-20260309-v2) increased kernel preemption/granularity causing more context-switch stalls when combined with batching patterns for x-small-v1.
- Secondary contributing factor: autoscaler probe timeout (health-check) set too aggressive, leading to slow-reacting scale-up during bursty traffic.
- Evidence: node logs show repeated kernel-level schedule_backoff() events correlated with GPU driver logs; no application-level errors.

Hotfix packaging checklist (minimal safe set):
- Branch: reverts: kernel-scheduling-flag; patch: autoscaler probe timeout 3s->6s; config: max_batch_size override rollback for model family x-small-v1.
- Tests: run canary bench (local perf harness) with seq lengths 128, 512, 1024 for 30m. Compare p95/p99 and GPU queuing metrics vs baseline.
- PR: include profiling snapshot (Flame graphs), node logs, and results of the canary bench. Link PR -> JIRA RE-3421.
- Deployment: canary to 4 nodes in us-west pool (non-prod label), wait 20m + manual sign-off by release engineer. If stable, ramp to 25% traffic, wait 40m, then full ramp.

Canary thresholds (stop and roll back if any triggers):
- p99 increases >20% vs baseline for 20m window.
- request_error_rate increases >0.5% absolute.
- GPU queue latency (kernel-side) remains above 200ms median.

Rollback decision tree (quick):
- If canary shows degradation -> immediate rollback to previous image and re-enable previous autoscaler probe. Notify on-call for postmortem.
- If canary improves but production shows intermittent anomalies -> hold and expand canary to other AZs before full rollout.
- If non-kernel causes identified -> escalate to infra-platform and pause rolling out this hotfix.

Release train coordination notes:
- This hotfix is tracked as a patch release on current release train; target window: 18:00 PDT (hotfix slot).
- Notify release-conductor (tag @release-conductor in Slack) when PR is ready and canary bench passes.
- For Dedicated customers, prepare Opt-out notice (small subset customers with pinned versions) — product needs to sign-off.

Observability & dashboards updated:
- Created temp dashboard: RE / Midday-latency-spike-20260310 (linked in artifacts).
- Added a short-lived alert: gpu_queue_tail_ms > 250ms -> PagerDuty SEV3 until hotfix ships.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Is the kernel-scheduling flag revert safe for all node types? (Action: Diego to validate on p4/rt nodes by 2026-03-11 EOD).
- Should we make max_batch_size dynamic per node pressure (as a medium-term fix)? (Product/Optimize team to evaluate).
- Are there any customers in Dedicated with strict latency SLOs who should be proactively notified? (CS to check customer list — Priya to follow up).

Action items (owners + due):
- Priya Rao: finalize hotfix PR and link JIRA RE-3421 (due 2026-03-10 16:00 PDT).
- Marcus Patel: smoke test rollback procedure in staging and document steps in playbook (due 2026-03-12).
- Diego Morales: validate kernel flag revert across node types + upload verification logs (due 2026-03-11 EOD).
- Ava Thompson: implement a temporary dynamic batching guard (prototype) and demo in eng sandbox (due 2026-03-17).
- Sophie Nguyen: coordinate release-conductor sign-off and update release calendar (due 2026-03-10 17:00 PDT).

Retrospective notes (initial):
- What worked: fast routing fallback + small config change (batch size) quickly reduced tail. Canary bench + clear thresholds defined made decision simpler.
- What didn't: kernel bump landed upstream without sufficient perf smoke for our batching patterns; autoscaler probe defaults were too aggressive. A pre-merge perf check for node images should be added to release flow.

Draft checklist for future prevention:
- Add kernel image perf smoke tests that include typical batching workloads (x-small-v1 patterns) as part of image promotion pipeline.
- Add a canary probe for autoscaler that simulates bursty traffic once per image boot.
- Add runbook entry: "if p99 tail increases without error rate, check GPU queue metrics first" with troubleshooting steps.

Notes to next shift (handoff):
- Watch dashboard RE / Midday-latency-spike-20260310 for 48 hours.
- If new spikes appear and linked artifacts point to different nodes, escalate to infra-platform.
- Current state: hotfix PR in progress (RE-HOTFIX-198) and canary bench scheduled; baseline restored after mitigations.

Appendix (quick links and artifacts):
- Perf graphs: attached to PR RE-HOTFIX-198 (artifact id: perf-20260310-01).
- Node trace bundle: s3://redwood-ops/artifacts/trace-20260310-01.tar.gz
- Slack thread: #release-engineering (thread ts=1646990000.000200)
- JIRA: RE-3421 (hotfix tracking), RE-3423 (postmortem follow-up tasks)

-- End of handoff --

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc lightweight; prefer linking to PR & dashboard rather than duplicating large logs.
- If hotfix slips past the 18:00 window, re-evaluate customer impact and consider emergency patch window.

Unresolved: whether the scheduling flag revert changes GPU memory behavior under extreme batching; re-check memory pressure metrics during canary.
